headline: Google fixes actively exploited Android zero-day on Pixel devices
summary: Google released September 2026 patches for 110 vulnerabilities on Pixel devices, including an actively exploited Android zero‑day.
whyItMatters: The flaw is being used in targeted attacks against Pixel users.
recommendedAction: Apply the September 2026 security update to all Pixel devices immediately.

headline: Attackers Exploit WooCommerce Wholesale Lead Capture Flaw to Plant PHP Web Shells
summary: Threat actors are exploiting a critical unauthenticated file‑upload vulnerability in the WooCommerce Wholesale Lead Capture plugin to install PHP web shells and achieve remote code execution.
whyItMatters: The flaw can compromise any WordPress site using the plugin, exposing data and servers.
recommendedAction: Update or remove the plugin and apply any available patches immediately.

headline: Active Exploitation Attempts Target WSO2 API Manager JWT Bypass With Forged Admin Tokens
summary: A critical JWT authentication bypass (CVE‑2026‑5430) in WSO2 API Manager is being actively exploited to forge admin tokens and potentially take over accounts.
whyItMatters: Successful exploitation could allow attackers full control over API management infrastructure.
recommendedAction: Apply the vendor’s patch for CVE‑2026‑5430 and rotate all admin tokens.

headline: Acronis warns of actively exploited flaw in its cPanel backup plugin
summary: Acronis disclosed a high‑severity local privilege escalation vulnerability in its backup plugin for cPanel, WHM, and Plesk that is being exploited in the wild.
whyItMatters: Attackers could gain root access on affected servers, compromising all hosted data.
recommendedAction: Update the backup plugin to the patched version and monitor for suspicious activity.

headline: Malcious Admin Menu Editor Pro plugin backdoors 1,500 WordPress sites
summary: Compromised versions of the Admin Menu Editor Pro WordPress plugin were distributed to over 200 customers, creating hidden user accounts that backdoored more than 1,500 sites.
whyItMatters: The hidden accounts allow attackers persistent access to a large number of WordPress installations.
recommendedAction: Remove the malicious plugin version, change all admin credentials, and scan for backdoors.

headline: KREMLIN Banking Malware Hijacks Chrome and Edge to Steal Credentials and Session Tokens
summary: The KREMLIN banking malware toolkit hijacks Chrome and Edge browsers to steal credentials and session tokens, targeting Brazilian bank customers since at least May 2025.
whyItMatters: It enables financial theft from victims by capturing authentication data.
recommendedAction: Deploy endpoint protection, block malicious extensions, and advise users to reinstall browsers.

headline: CenterPoint Energy confirms customer data stolen in cyberattack
summary: CenterPoint Energy disclosed that a cyberattack resulted in the theft of personal information of some customers.
whyItMatters: Exposed personal data can lead to identity theft and regulatory penalties.
recommendedAction: Notify affected customers, monitor for fraud, and strengthen security controls.

headline: Iranian Hackers Use Telegram-Controlled Malware to Spy on Dissidents and Journalists
summary: Iranian intelligence‑linked hackers use a Windows malware controlled via Telegram to exfiltrate emails, chats, screenshots, and microphone recordings from dissidents and journalists.
whyItMatters: The tool enables state‑sponsored surveillance of targeted individuals worldwide.
recommendedAction: Advise at‑risk users to avoid suspicious files and monitor network traffic for Telegram callbacks.

headline: BambooToken Malware Uses MQTT to Control Windows and Linux Systems
summary: Researchers identified the BambooToken malware family, which uses the MQTT protocol to command and control compromised Windows and Linux systems across Asia and South America.
whyItMatters: MQTT‑based C2 can bypass traditional detection methods, expanding the threat surface.
recommendedAction: Monitor network for unusual MQTT traffic and block unauthorized brokers.

headline: BambooToken malware controls Windows and Linux systems via MQTT
summary: A previously unknown malware framework called BambooToken uses the MQTT protocol to communicate with and control Windows and Linux systems.
whyItMatters: Its use of MQTT creates a stealthy command channel that evades many security tools.
recommendedAction: Detect and block unauthorized MQTT communications and isolate infected hosts.
